sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State
Counsel for Revisionist :- P.P.Srivastava,K.K. Singh,R.K. Chaudhary
Counsel for Opposite Party :- A.G.A.
Hon'ble Sudhir Agarwal,J.
1.
Called in revise.
None appeared to press this revision.
In the circumstances, I myself have perused the record.
2. This criminal revision under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C., has been filed aggrieved by the judgments and orders dated 18.10.1985 and 19.08.1988.

The Special Judicial Magistrate (Economic Offences),
Basti vide order dated 18.10.1985 passed in Criminal Case No. 1055 of 1984 convicted revisionists and sentenced them for two years rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs. 2000/- under Section 7/16 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as ?Act, 1954?) and further for two months rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs. 3000/- under Section 7/16(1)A1(II) of Act, 1954.
Thereagainst, revisionist preferred Criminal Appeal No. 100 of 1985 and Appellate Court while dismissing appeal has confirmed the conviction and sentence passed by Trial Court.
Being aggrieved the revisionist preferred present revision.

sentences.text:
Having gone through the record, I do not find any manifest error or otherwise illegality,
procedural or otherwise, so as to justify interference in criminal revision.
4. Dismissed.
Interim order, if any, stands vacated.
5. The accused, Gyan Dass and Mahesh Kumar, are on bail.
Their bail bonds and surety bonds are cancelled.
The Chief Judicial Magistrate concerned shall cause them to be arrested and lodge in jail to serve out the sentence passed against them.
The compliance shall be prepared within two months.
6. Certify this judgment to the lower Court immediately.
